note: A search that returns nothing is only worth anything if the search itself is written down. Every query below was actually run, on the date given, and its result is recorded whether or not it helped.

sets.g: FamilySearch Full-Text — four South African collections this archive had never opened
sets.n: a name-indexed land register, and Booyzen in it
rows: Full-text search, q.text=Barry Kolbe, South Africa

The first hope was that full-text search — which reads unindexed images rather than volunteer indexes — could reach the two missing Barry children. It cannot. South African full-text coverage does NOT include the Dutch Reformed church registers. That is a clean negative and it closes the last screen route to those two children.

What the coverage DOES include, and what this archive has never once searched: VOTER RECORDS, SOUTH AFRICA, VOTING RECORDS 1925–1931 · DE LIST, CAPE PROVINCE, MILITARY RECORDS 1901–1903 · LAND RECORDS, SOUTH AFRICA, FARM RECORDS 1895 and 1895–1955. The military one lands on the Anglo-Boer War years and the rebel question; the land ones land on Question 11, the farm. All four are full-text searchable, which is a different kind of access from anything this archive has used.
RAK 2508, “Ewaton Book 2” — the land-register index, images 14 and 15

An alphabetical index in three columns, SURNAME · CHRISTIAN NAME · FOLIO, read from the image and not from the AI transcript, which is unreliable. The Booyzen block reads: “Booyzen · Catharine Mary [S…] · 2492” and “Jacobus Nicolaas · 201”; “Booijzen · Matthys Joh… · 1866”; “Booijzen · Jacobus Nicholas · 2267”; “Booyzen · Jacobus Nicolaas · 1931, 1939”. TWO OF THOSE NAMES ARE IN THIS ARCHIVE. Jacobus Nicolaas Booyzen is the eldest of the eight on the 1863 death notice, who “ended in the Transvaal” with estate TAB MHG 52653 and nothing else attached to him — and Evaton is in the Transvaal. The Catharine Mary reading is the family's signature female name and the hardest of the four to be sure of. NOTHING IS ADOPTED: a surname in a land index is not an identification, the folios have not been followed, and the ledgers those folios point into are a different volume from this index.
RAK 2384, Wonderboom South — the folios followed into a transfer register

Image 219 of 261, image group 121082126. A deeds transfer register for WONDERBOOM SOUTH, which is Pretoria — the district where David Schalk Booysen was living at GOEDEHOOP when he remarried in November 1905. Three rows carry the name. (1) “E. S. D. Gey van Pittius (gel. Schulte)” to PETRUS JACOBUS BOOYZEN, 1939, £25. (2) “Boedel wyle P. J. BOOYZEN” — the estate of the late P.J. Booyzen — to MAGDALENA JOHANNA BOOYZEN. (3) “M. J. BOOYZEN (born BEZUIDENHOUT), Wed.” to DAVID SCHALK BOOYZEN, 9 APRIL 1907. The household reads Petrus Jacobus, David Schalk, Magdalena Johanna — which is this archive's direct line name for name, and is exactly why it is being written down as a lead and not as a finding. NOT PROVED AND NOT ADOPTED. If the David Schalk of April 1907 were this archive's David Schalk Booysen, born Cradock 1848, it would carry him seventeen months past the last date held for him and give him land; but the transferor is a widow born Bezuidenhout and this archive's man married a widow born Stols, so the household may be a different branch entirely. The next step is the deed itself, not this ledger line.

sets.g: FamilySearch, back after two days — the queued queries, and one that paid
sets.n: the 1788 baptism is not in the index; a nine-child household is
rows: The decisive record — the baptism of 21 September 1788, which names the father and would settle de Villiers against the 1876 Sterfkennis — does NOT surface. The endpoint returns 19th and 20th century entries regardless of the birthLikeDate range, and the same happened with anyDate on Graaff-Reinet. This is consistent with what Question 0 already says: the 18th-century Cape registers are not name-indexed and have to be read page by page. NOT a negative about the register, a negative about the index.

The mother filter did not bite and the wildcard dragged in Dutch Booijink and Booijman families. But two entries land squarely on de Villiers' page 78: Petrus Jacobus Booijzen, born 1814, of GERRIT BOOIJZEN and ANNA ELISABETH THERON; and Anna Susanna Booijze, baptised 12 May 1805 at Graaff-Reinet, of JAN JONATHAN BOOIJZE and JUDITH CORNELIA ETRESIA VILJOEN. The book gives Jan's sons Gerrit married to Anna Elisabeth Theron in 1791 and Jan Jonathan married to Judith Cornelia Theresia Viljoen in 1797. TWO OF JAN'S SONS CONFIRMED FROM RECORDS, independently of the book — which raises what the book says about the third son, Petrus Jacobus.

The query Question 13 named as untried. It does not answer which two of the eleven are missing — these are grandchildren, not children — but it hands this archive a family it did not have at all. John Augustus Barry II, who was a name on two death notices with no wife and no issue, married ALIDA JACOBA VAN ELLINCKHUIZEN and had NINE children baptised at Burgersdorp and then Dordrecht, 1871 to 1889. The eldest is a THIRD Catherine Mary Sophia. The seventh is ANTON RECTOR KOLBE BARRY — the Kolbe name in a fourth generation, sixty-two years after the Settler landed. A fourth John Augustus appears at ELLIOT by 1908, the same village where Henry James Booyzen married in 1912.
The two 1848 Barry index entries, opened and compared

Henry Jaonas Barry (baptism indexed 13 Nov 1868) and Hennery James Berry (baptism indexed 13 Nov 1848) share a birth date of 13 July 1848, share parents John Barry and Margret Willemina Kolbe, sit in the same collection, and are BOTH attached in the FamilySearch tree to one person: James Henry Barry, 1848–1939, L6J6-JHX. The film's own title closes the question — “Graaff-Reinet. Baptism Records 1846–1851” cannot contain an 1868 baptism. Gained: an exact birth and baptism for James Henry Barry, and the correct place, Graaff-Reinet, against the Cape Town and Tulbagh the index gives. Lost: the tenth-child candidate. Image located, apid:TH-909-70517-31299-17, and NOT yet read.
Film 008119684, image 930 — the entry itself, read

“603 · Het Kind is N. HENRY JAMES · Get. 13 July 1848 · Gedoopt 13 Novr 1848 · V. John Barry · M. Margret Willemina Kolber · Gt: Petrus Jacobus Joubert, CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER.” The year is 1848 in the clerk's hand, the forename order is HENRY JAMES rather than James Henry, and the godmother — whom this archive held as plain “Catharine Kolbe” — carries CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA eleven years before her sister gave it to the daughter this archive had been treating as the head of that chain. The namesakes page called it a Barry name. It is a Kolbe name.
q.motherSurname=Olivier · q.fatherGivenName=Hendrik Stef* — the three untraced daughters, again

The relationship search that worked on the Kolbes fails here, and the reason is worth writing down: OLIVIER is common enough, and “Hendrik Stefanus” frequent enough as a forename pair, that the engine returns Strydoms, Le Rouxs and Rossouws from Jamestown to Oudtshoorn and not one member of this household. A method is not a key; it works where the names are rare. Anna Johanna Maria, Elesabettha Maria Cornelya and Magdalena Johanna Booijsen remain exactly where they were.
Film 008119684, image 876 — John Augustus Barry II's font, 1847

Entry 80: “Het Kind N. JOHN AUGUST · Get. 13 Maart 1847 · Gedoopt 12 April 1847 · V. JOHN BERRY · M. MARGARETWINA KOLBE · Gt: JOHN KOLBE, MARGARET KOLBE, AUGUSTA KOLBE” — the third witness the least certain of the three. Read with entry 603 of the year after, where the godmother is Catharine Sophia Maria Kolbe, the pattern is plain: at both fonts every witness is a Kolbe, and the forenames this archive has been calling Barry names are the names of the people standing at them.
q.surname=B*rry · q.motherSurname=Kolb* and Col* — every spelling the index uses
Seven children, and four known ones missing

The mother is indexed as Kolbe, Kolber, Kolbee, Colbe, Colby and Colbee, and her forenames run Margret Willemina, Margret Lowisa, Margaretha Louisa Willemina, Margarita Elizabeth Willemina and Margerite Elizabeth Wellemina. Sweeping all of them returns SEVEN baptisms — 1847, 1848, 1850, 1853, 1859, 1861, 1863 — and not one name this archive did not already hold. THE IMPORTANT PART IS WHAT IS ABSENT: Hendrik Nicholaas, Richard Peter, Margaret Mary and Kathleen Mary are all NAMED ON THEIR PARENTS' DEATH NOTICES and none of the four is in the index. So the index cannot find four children this archive knows existed, which settles that it will not find the two it does not. This route is CLOSED, and closed for a demonstrable reason rather than a discouraging one. What is left is the registers themselves — Graaff-Reinet, Burgersdorp and Dordrecht — read across the gaps at 1851-1852, 1854-1858 and after 1864.
The register that would settle it, located and measured

The two missing Barry children, if they were born in the gap, are in a single volume: BURGERSDORP. BAPTISM RECORDS 1852–1866, image group 008039088, 534 images — it covers 1854 to 1858 entire, and the years on either side. Landmarks for bisecting it: 1853 is at IMAGE 54 (entry for William Fredrik Barry, 23 October), and 1866 is at IMAGE 528. That is roughly 36 images a year, which puts the 1854–1858 gap at about IMAGES 70 TO 250. There is NO NAME INDEX at the back — 528 onward are ordinary 1866 entries. NOT YET READ: this is a sequential browse of some 150 images and it was not attempted in the session that located it, deliberately, because the viewer's image-number box does not reliably move the single-image view (the grid view does jump, and is the way in). Written down so the job resumes rather than restarts.

sets.g: Queensland's historical index — did any branch reach Australia before the living generation?
sets.n: eleven surnames, and not one of this family
rows: familyhistory.bdm.qld.gov.au · subjectfamilyname=BOOYZEN · births, marriages and deaths
The spelling this archive uses does not occur once in Queensland's register between 1829 and 1996. Neither does BOOYSENS, nor SLIER, nor SCHOEMAN.

Betty Beatrice Booysen, who died in 1977, was born an Appleby of English parents. Jasper van Graan Booysen, who died in 1994, is the son of Hendrik Hermanes Booysen and Dorothea Catharina van Graan — an Afrikaans household, and a real one, but no Hendrik Hermanes and no van Graan appears anywhere in this archive. A shared surname and a shared country of origin are not a join.
· MOUNTJOY, KOLBE, DASCHNER, PRETORIUS, OLIVIER, ENGELBRECHT, ENSLIN

The Queensland Kolbes are a German Catholic family who married Wiemers and Thurners at Toowoomba. The Queensland Daschners descend from Josef Daschner and Fany Wagner, Bavarians — not from Joseph Heinrich Daschner of Stutterheim. Most OLIVIER hits are the word used as a given name, in the Barkus family. The Pretorius rows are Afrikaans and unconnected: Ben Johannes Pretorius married Edith Watts Treasure at Brisbane in 1918, and neither name is in this archive.

Queensland's index covers births to 1926, marriages to 1951 and deaths to 1996. Across that whole span no member of this family registered a birth, a marriage or a death in Queensland. The family's arrival in Brisbane is as recent as this archive says it is, and there was no earlier Australian branch to find.
Boijens-9 and De_Beer-638 — following the contradiction one generation up

Jan Booysen married Magdalena de Beer on 21 January 1770 and married again on 15 DECEMBER 1793, so his wife was dead by then; this archive's Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer died in 1843. Fifty years apart, which is the objection Question 0 raised against the 1793 will when it declined to adopt it — the reasoning was right, and the will is now positively HIS. The tree's own de Beer profile explains the rest: codes b6c2 AND b6c6, baptisms in 1745 and 1754, and a sibling list holding both a Magdalena and a Magdalena Elizabeth. Two women merged into one profile. Gained: a candidate for our woman's parents, Zaccharias de Beer and Anna Pretorius, and a second printed reference, de Villiers and Pama Vol 1 p. 78.
The Booysen surname index on WikiTree, and the parent-field search

The Booyzen index holds 13 profiles; the BOOYSEN index holds 952, and this family lives in both — Booysen-267 and Booysen-293 were reached by following parent links, not by searching. Swept for Gerthardus, Gerhardus, Lodewikus, Willem Hermanus, Jacobus Nicolaas, Ockert, and for all Booysens born at Graaff-Reinet. NO Gerthardus Booysen exists on WikiTree at all. One near-name worth keeping: Jan Gerhardus Lodewikus Booysen (1871–1920, a different family) — proof that JAN and GERHARDUS LODEWIKUS travel together as forenames in this surname.
Heese, Suid-Afrikaanse Geslagsregisters — a route that does not wait on the forum

WorldCat gates its results behind an acceptance of OCLC's terms, which this archive will not click through. Trove returned nothing for the title in Books & Libraries, so no Australian holding was identified. The realistic routes left are the Genealogical Society of South Africa and eGGSA, or the G2G question already posted. Recorded as tried and unresolved rather than untried.
de Villiers 1893, read in full instead of asked about
Four agree, the father does not

Pieter van Zyl answered the G2G question within a day and named the book as downloadable. It was downloaded from archive.org and read rather than trusted. Page 34 confirms his answer exactly: Zacharias is the FIFTH child of Matthijs Andries (b5, not WikiTree's b6), and it is the 1754 Magdalena, not the 1745 one, that carries “zie Booijsen”. Page 78 then gives Petrus Jacobus of 21 September 1788 as the seventh child of JAN Booijsen and that Magdalena, with David Schalk of 4 January 1807 as his son. One Petrus Jacobus of that date in the book, one David Schalk of that date, and no Lodewikus anywhere in the volume.

sets.g: WikiTree, never once opened in this project until somebody asked
sets.n: thirteen profiles read — one page number, four facts, one head-on contradiction
rows: The archive had eleven MyHeritage trees, Geni and the FamilySearch tree listed under “Other trees holding this family”, and the word WikiTree appeared nowhere in the project. Of the thirteen Booyzen profiles, FIVE are this family: Petrus Jacobus (1788), David Schalk, Hendrik Stefanus, Henry James and Jacobus Nicolaas.
Booysen-267 — Petrus Jacobus, b. bef 21 Sep 1788, d. 1 Sep 1876

Identical birth and death dates to this archive's man, and the parents given as JAN (Boijens) BOOYSEN and MAGDALENA DE BEER against this archive's GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS BOOIJSEN and Magdalena de Beer, which come off line 3 of the 1876 Sterfkennis No. 678. Same mother, same son, two husbands. The profile cites HEESE, SUID-AFRIKAANSE GESLAGSREGISTERS, DEEL 1, P. 331 — the book Question 0 has named from the start and never had a page number for. Nothing changed: a read document outranks a tree.
Booysen-293 — Hendrik Stefanus, d. 11 May 1908 Rustenburg

Age at death “79 & 11 months”, the 1850 Potchefstroom marriage to Anna Johanna Olivier, then Charlotta Dormehl at Zeerust — all matching. Its parentage line reads “Elizabetha ? (Anna Maria ?) van der Merwe”: another researcher reached this archive's oldest contradiction and left it as a question mark. The 1908 death notice, TAB 14380, settles it as Elizabetha.
Booyzen-12 and Booyzen-11 — Henry James and Jacobus Nicolaas

Henry James born 12 August 1887 (this archive had “c. 1887” off a burial age) and married Dorothea Regina Barry on 17 June 1912 AT ELLIOT. Jacobus Nicolaas married Jacomina Jacoba Jansen van Rensburg on 12 February 1866 at Middelburg — a wife this archive did not have at all, though the profile's own source line dates that marriage 1899. All FROM A TREE, none adopted into the family data.

Son of Jan Hendrik Booysen and Cornelia Margaretha Voetzé, and married three times — the first of them, on the profile's own figures, at TWELVE YEARS OLD. Ruled out, and worth recording as the reason a name match is not an identification.
Henry James Booyzen's profile sources — “Form of information of death”

Estate MHG 10/57 is one of the six files on the FamilySearch films that refuse images, and it is in the letter to the National Archives in Pretoria. The WikiTree profile manager cites a death notice for the same man. That is a person who has seen a document this archive cannot reach.

Question 2082757, “Has anyone seen the sterfkennis in Transvaal estate MHG 10/57 (Booyzen, 1956)?”, in Genealogy Help under south_africa, south_african_roots, booysen and death_notice — the four tags that actually carry traffic, checked against live G2G rather than guessed. It asks for the parents, birthplace, occupation and children off the one document that would settle Henry James Booyzen, and offers the Johannesburg cemetery entry in exchange. Nothing has come back yet and this row will say so until something does.

sets.g: Three questions put to the index directly — and one that answered back
sets.n: three negatives and one name the notices never gave
rows: Her mother's 1891 estate 6332 returns her persona and nothing else — no baptism, no marriage, no death, no estate. Elesabettha Maria Cornelya Booijsen exists in this archive because a clerk listed her among seven children in 1891, and after this search she still exists on that single line. The other two untraced Olivier daughters return the same nothing.
q.surname=Booij* · q.motherGivenName=Elizabetha · q.motherSurname=Van der Merwe · births 1824–1840

The search asks the index for anyone born to Petrus Jacobus Booijzen and Elizabetha van der Merwe across the whole plausible span of their marriage. It returns other Booijens and Booijzen households and not one child of theirs. If she bore children who were baptised, the register carrying them is not indexed.

This was the direct test. His own baptism would have named both his parents in one line and settled her in a second document. It is not there — the only return is Q29M-ZJGY, the 1850 Potchefstroom marriage this archive already has. So ELIZABETHA VAN DER MERWE still rests on exactly one piece of paper: the 1908 death notice of her son. Three routes tried, three closed.
One new name, one already held

John Barry's 1903 registration says ELEVEN children; his notice names eight and his wife's names nine. This query — asking the index for every Barry child of a Kolbe mother rather than for a person — returns the known ones and two that are on neither notice. Only ONE of the two is new. WILLIAM FREDERICK THOMAS BARRY, baptised 29 September 1861, was already on William Barry's page, entered the day the Burgersdorp register was read; this archive wrote him up as a find for an hour before checking its own data, and the correction is logged. The new name is HENRY JAONAS BARRY, born 13 July 1848 and baptised at twenty years old on 13 November 1868 — a date that fits the sixteen-month gap after John Augustus II better than the “about 1847” this archive carries for James Henry. INDEX ONLY, double-indexed to two villages, and nothing has been added to the family on it. The register has to be read.
The same query, re-run for the record identifiers

FamilySearch closed the window after two calls, and unlike every other refusal this week it did not reopen. Waits of four, twenty-five, thirty and forty seconds all returned 403, and the block then spread off the search service and onto the site itself — an ordinary results page loaded in a browser with a body of ZERO characters. Nearly an hour of rests did not clear it. So the record identifiers needed to reach the two baptism images were never retrieved, and the relationship search run on the FATHER instead of the mother — the obvious next query, and the one with a real chance at the second missing child — was never run at all. Marked BLOCKED and not NOTHING: the index was not asked.

sets.g: David Schalk Booysen after November 1905 — and the rest of the 1876 eight
sets.n: both negative
rows: DAVID SCHALK BOOYSEN, born 9 June 1848 — his death

Alive and fifty-six at GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA on 27 November 1905, and this archive loses him there. No estate file in the indexed Transvaal probate records — the only David Schalk Booyzen there is a CHILD on the 1940 Stephanus Francois estate. No civil death that can be him: the candidates are a Cradock man born 1870, a Rustenburg man born 1859 (eleven years out), a Pretoria man born 1907 and a Clayville man born 1889. The 1859 Rustenburg death of 7 March 1930 is the nearest and is NOT adopted.
The other seven children of Petrus Jacobus Booysen and Anna Maria van der Merwe

Searched by MOTHER (Anna Maria van der Merwe) and by FATHER (Petrus/Pieter Jacobus Booijzen) across 1806–1830 in all South African collections. Exactly ONE comes back — DAVID SCHALK, born 12 December 1806. The other seven of the eight on the 1876 Sterfkennis are not in the indexed baptism registers under either parent. The 1876 notice remains the only document that names them at all.
Rechecked. His 1918 registration says MARRIED; the civil marriage index carries no Richard Peter Booyzen who can be him.
JOHANNA ELENA STOLS, his second wife — her death

The last route to his death date: a widow's notice names her pre-deceased husband. Searched under BOOYZEN, BOOYSEN and LOWIES for any death 1906–1945. Nothing that can be her. So the route is CLOSED, not merely untried — neither David Schalk Booysen nor his second wife has a findable death, and the trail ends at Goedehoop in November 1905. Added to the Pretoria errand as an index search rather than a file request.

sets.g: Following the estate numbers out of a marriage register's last column
sets.n: 2 for 2
rows: Elizabetha Margaretha Booijzen, born Marais — the death notice that opened David Schalk Booysen's whole household. Read entire.

Charles Petrus Barend Lowies, born district Cradock about 1849, died Pretoria 5 June 1905, twelve children, parents Jan Lowies and Elisabetha Maria Lubbe. The IMAGE was not opened: FamilySearch began refusing record-page requests part-way through the session — “Access Denied, Error 15, this request was blocked by our security service”.

His 1918 death registration says MARRIED, so there is a widow. The South African civil marriage index carries no Richard Peter Booyzen who can be him — the Richards it does carry belong to other families. She has no name.

sets.g: The Johannesburg Booyzens who are NOT claimed
sets.n: 4 tested, 0 adopted
rows: Petrus Jacobus Booyzen, b. May 1882, d. May 1961, buried Johannesburg

The best of the four. A birth in May 1882 would make him Kathleen Barry's eldest, ahead of John Barry in 1884, and Petrus Jacobus is the most-repeated forename this family has. That is a name and a gap, and there is no document.
Petrus Jacobus VAN BLERK Booyzen, b. 1872, d. 17 Mar 1949, West Park
VAN BLERK is a mother's surname carried as a forename and there is no Van Blerk anywhere in this family. A different Booyzen household on the Rand.
Jan Gerhardus Lodewikus Booysen, buried Johannesburg 17 Dec 1943

The name is exactly right — it runs from Gerthardus Lodewikus at the top of this line to the man who died at Vaalbank in 1885. But the 1855 child of that name would be 88 in 1943, the register gives NO AGE, and the name is common in the wider family.
John Zacharia Booysen, d. 25 Nov 1918, buried Brixton 26 Nov, aged 29

ZACHARIA reaches nothing in this family, and his death is a civil registration which names no parents, so nothing could tie him either way. Recorded only because three Booysens went into Brixton in eight weeks in the influenza and the shape of that is worth keeping.
Richard Peter Booyzen, d. 25 Oct 1918, Turffontein

The one that IS adopted, and on three grounds and no document: his mother's brother's forename; a birth about 1894 in the exact gap in her children; and a birthplace of C. OF G. HOPE on the registration, which is the migration all her children made.

sets.g: The Grahamstown depot, swept for Barry, Mountjoy and Booyzen
sets.n: two estates, both already read
rows: BARRY, exact surname, probate at Grahamstown / Albany

All of them are ONE document — John Barry's own 1915 notice, estate 925, which this archive has read entire. The index even carries NEAGLE BARRY as a person, which is the surname the informant gave for his grandmother and could not follow with a Christian name. The rest of the Grahamstown Barrys — Van Reenen, Dirk Gysbert, Durban, Phyllis, Thomas — are a different Barry family on the same film.
MOUNTJOY, exact surname, probate at Grahamstown / Albany

John James Mountjoy 1923 and a George Mountjoy family group of 1919–20 (Susan Elizabeth, d. 13 Sep 1920 at Mt Prospect, Flagstaff, b. 1887 Maclear; with Ivy Elizabeth, Gwendoline Hazel, Edna Iris and Daphne Joyce). Flagstaff and Maclear are Transkei, a different Mountjoy household, and NOT ADOPTED.
BOOYZEN, exact surname, probate at Grahamstown / Albany
January, Jonas, Sarah, Martha, Meetje, Aletta, Johanna, G — Middelburg and Basutoland, 1850 to 1920. A different Booyzen family entirely and this archive does not claim them.
a finding aid, not an absence

Margaretha Kolbe's probate was GRANTED AT GRAHAMSTOWN and is INDEXED UNDER KIMBERLEY. Three earlier searches for it failed because they trusted the collection label. A depot sweep that searches by place will not find a record filed under the wrong one.

sets.g: The Marico question, re-run on the grandsons — and the reason for dismissing it withdrawn
sets.n: initials still fail, district objection dead
rows: The seven TAB CJC claims — JPJ, PJ, GL, JPJ, L, JC, HE — against the GRANDSONS, who are now named

This archive could not run this test in September because it could not name a single grandson. It can now: PJ (Petrus Jacobus, b. 20 Apr 1851), OJS (Ockert Johannes Stephanus, b. 15 Sep 1852), AJM, EMC, ACJ, MJ and HSN (Hendrik Stefanus Nicolaas, b. 31 Jan 1862, DEAD IN 1891) from the first marriage; and in the next generation PJ (1889), OJS (1894), HSN (1882) and DA (Diederik Arnoldus, 1887). Against JPJ, PJ, GL, JPJ, L, JC, HE only PJ fits, and Petrus Jacobus is the commonest name this family has. The initials test still fails.
BUT: the ground the dismissal stood on

The reason given for setting the seven Marico claims aside was “that is NOT this family, who were Cape”. That sentence is now false twice over. HENDRIK STEFANUS BOOIJZEN MARRIED AT ZEERUST, THE PRINCIPAL TOWN OF MARICO, ON 14 APRIL 1892; and his wife CHARLOTTA ELIZABETH DORMEHL lived at DRIEFONTEIN, GROOT MARICO and DIED THERE ON 6 FEBRUARY 1902 — during the war, in the district the claims come from. He signed her death notice at Zeerust in August 1902. This family was in Marico, documented, on both sides of the war.

The claims are still not tied to a named man. What has gone is the excuse for not looking. The CJC series is not name-indexed and the seven claims are numbers — CJC 76, 77, 104, 109, 123, 125, 126 — that only the Reading Room can open.
And a compensation claim that DOES exist
Not in Marico. DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, at Pretoria, answering question ten of his wife's 1900 death notice: “none. Compensation claim filed.” See /documents/#marais-1900.

sets.g: Johannesburg cemetery registers — the whole family, swept
sets.n: 298 read
rows: Booyzen · Booysen · Booijzen · Daschner · Mountjoy · Lerena, exact surname, collection 4453927

Ten of them are this family and each turns a year into a day: Kathleen Barry (grave 9760), Willem Hermanus of Indwe and Susanna Adriana (grave 6889, together), Henry James, Joseph Heinrich Daschner, Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas, George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen, George Downing Daschner, and two infants at Brixton the archive did not have.
The index rows carry name, age, date and cemetery; the grave number is on the register image, and only two have been read page by page so far. The rest are a morning's work.

Richard Peter Booyzen, 24, buried 27 October 1918 at Brixton — claimed as kin on the naming and the gap in the children, marked INFERRED. John Zacharia Booysen, 29, buried 26 November, and Johanna A. Booysen, nought days, on 19 December: NOT claimed. No forename in this family reaches them and Booysen is common on the Rand.

sets.g: Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen (1852–1921) — an estate of his own
sets.n: no file
rows: Transvaal probate index — Ockert / Okkert / Ocker / Ocken against Booysen / Booyzen / Booijsen

Every hit is him as somebody else's relative: four duplicate copies of his son Diederik Arnoldus's 1935 Sterfkennis 87882, where he is the father; and two copies of his own father's 1908 notice 14380, where he is entered Child.

OKKER JOHANNIS STEPHANUS BOOYSEN, 69, died 16 January 1921 at Klerksdorp. A civil registration NAMES NO PARENTS — which is the whole difficulty with this series and why the archive keeps going back to Sterfkennisse.
Browsing the films for 1921 by estate number
The Transvaal probate films are not ordered by estate number, so there is nothing to browse along. If an estate was raised for him it is not name-indexed.

sets.n: the gap
rows: What this archive searched, every time, for the whole project.

What it should have searched. 145 documents unseen. This family left the Cape about 1907 and the entire last generation died in Johannesburg, so their estates are in the TRANSVAAL depot — and NAAIRS offers an “All Archives Repositories” database on the same selection page used every time.

BOOYZEN, JOHANNA MARIA born PRETORIUS (2945/44); BOOYZEN, GEORGE DOWNING MOUNTJOY (1095/48); BOOYZEN, JOHN BARRY (769/52) — the son who signed the 1905 form; BOOYZEN, HENRY JAMES (10/57); and DASCHNER, CATHERINE MARY SOPHIA born BOOYZEN (3734/46).
TAB MHG — two of the 1863 children
BOOYZEN, JAN GERHARDUS LODEWIKUS (O/2899, 1885), the seventh child; and BOOYZEN, JACOBUS NICHOLS (52653, 1923), the eldest and the only “Major” on that list.
TAB MHG — both sons of the second marriage
BOOYZEN, STEPHANUS FRANCOIS (2428/40) and BOOYZEN, GERT JACOBUS (5155/51). Both filed with a z.
Still no estate for Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen née Barry, who died at Mayfair in 1940. Her “Military Pensioner” entry remains unexplained.
TAB CJC — Claims for Compensation, Burghers

The post-war compensation series Open Question 11 has been asking for. It exists. But all seven claims are MARICO, Transvaal — the same district as the Booyzen children who died in the camps — and that is NOT this family, who were Cape. The series is now named correctly; the Cape equivalent is still untouched.

sets.g: National Archives · all repositories — three questions answered by absence
sets.n: RSA database
rows: There is NO estate file for Willem Hermanus Booyzen — the man at the centre of the family story — in any archives repository in South Africa. He died at Indwe in 1905 leaving nothing to administer. Set that beside his father's estate of 1884, which recorded "moveables only, such as wearing apparel": two generations, and between them not one estate worth opening.

The testimony ends "the boys initially all got jobs on the mines". No Booyzen mining record appears anywhere in the national archives index. That index covers GOVERNMENT files, not private mining company employment registers, so the negative is a weak one — but every occupation this archive has actually read for these men points elsewhere: boer then mason, tree nurseryman, clerk on the South African Railways. Not one miner among them.
The Johannesburg addresses appear on certificates but nowhere in the archival index.

SAB VWR B645/8/38 (1937): an application by a FARM OWNER AT BARKLY-OOS, R.P.K. BARRY, with his son of the same initials as bywoner. Given this family's Barry–Kolbe naming — Henry James Kolbe Barry, Anthon Rector Kolbe Barry — R.P.K. is very likely Richard Peter Kolbe Barry. That ties the Cape Rebel of Jerpoint, the R. P. Barry who signed the 1915 notice at Manorowen, and five mortgage bonds of 1895–1903 into one landholding man at Barkly East. Tighter, still not proof.
Still no estate anywhere for Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen née Barry, who died at Mayfair in 1940. Her “Military Pensioner” entry is now the longest-standing unexplained thing in the archive.

sets.n: 12,792 names

Nothing, in any of the fifteen registers.
And two of them are in this family's district: FRED J. BARRY of Ivanhoe, Barkly East / Wodehouse, tried June 1901; and RICHARD PETER BARRY of Jerpoint. Identity unproven.
DANIEL WILLEM SCHOEMAN, plaasboer of CAERLAVEROCK, tried June 1901 — the month before the family married in his house.

BOOYSEN + Catherine / Kathleen / John Barry / Willem Hermanus

sets.g: National Archives · Cape Town Archives Repository — the searches this archive got wrong first time
sets.n: a correction
rows: The archive previously reported MOUNTJOY as 42 documents of which “all 22 dated 1930 or later were read”. Twenty earlier documents were never opened. They include JAMES MOUNTJOY'S OWN WILLS of 1818 and 1827 and an 1834 Colonial Office memorial from his widow. A filter applied for convenience was written up as if it were the whole search.

KAB MOOC 7/1/104: 42 — MOUNTJOY, JAMES. WILL (1818), joint with SLIER, ANNA CATHARINA, WIFE OF JAMES MOUNTJOY; and MOOC 7/1/104: 43 — the same pair again in 1827, the year he died. Made a year after their 1817 marriage and again at his death.
KAB CO 3972: 17 — “MEMORIALS RECEIVED. THE WIDOW OF J MOUNTJOY. REQUESTING REMISSION OF A FINE”, 1834. A petition in her own voice, seven years after his death.

Five of them mortgage bonds in the name RICHARD PETER BARRY — 1895, 1897 twice, and 1903 twice. A property-holding farmer of that name in the Cape across the war years. Corroboration for the Cape Rebel of Jerpoint, not proof.
The farm name does not appear anywhere in the Cape Town Archives index.

One police constable at Middelburg, 1904–07, filed four times as BOOYSEN and three times as BOOYZEN — twice both ways inside 1905. The best evidence on this site for what the two spellings meant to the people writing them, and it narrows the archive's own reading of the 1905 death form.

sets.g: National Archives · Cape Town Archives Repository (NAAIRS)
sets.n: the KAB database
rows: All 22 dated 1930 or later were retrieved and read.
The spelling nobody had tried — and two of the four are the Mountjoy–Booysen junction itself, including the 1840 and 1863 death notices.
There is no estate file for Hercules Johannes Mountjoy under any spelling. The estates around him run 1938, 1939, 1943, 1946, 1948 unbroken, so this is an absence, not a gap in the index.
Earliest 1779 — KAB CJ 2633: 29, the testament of Christina Booyzen. The z is a hundred and twenty years older than the war.
No estate for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, d. 1843.
No estate for the man at the top of the male line.
All one later man, Willem Johannes Lodewicus.

One near-miss deliberately NOT adopted: KAB NCD 2/1: 49, a notarial will of 1793 for “Jan Booysen, married to the late Magdalena de Beer”. Wrong husband's name, and a wife dead fifty years before ours.

Behind a bot check. This archive did not attempt to circumvent it, and records that as the reason.

sets.g: Master of the Supreme Court · the office's own index of death notices, 1834–1912

The Magdalena entries are Magda Catha du Plessis (1872), Magda de Beer (1865), Magda Vermeulen (1883), Magda Eliz Troskie (1863), Magda Jacomina Nel (1850) and Magda Greef (1839/40). Page 436 onward, alphabetical by christian name with a death-notice number and year against each. A working index of every Booysen death notice reported to the Master between 1834 and 1912.

sets.n: for James Montjoy's origin
rows: Not tractable. The archive has no discriminator beyond a trade and a date — “a saddler, in the Cape by March 1817” — and thirteen thousand results cannot be narrowed by that. Recorded so the next person does not repeat it: the way in is a Cape arrival record, not an English birth record.

sets.g: FamilySearch · Transvaal estate films
sets.n: reading the nine located estates, one film at a time
rows: TAB MHG 2945/44 — Anna Johanna Maria Booyzen, born Pretorius

Indexed under her husband George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen as “Spouse”, which is why it was first mistaken for his estate. Sterfkennis, both parents named with a street address, six children with birth dates, all minors. One correction to the archive.
Seven of the nine still to open. References banked on the Sources page so this resumes rather than restarts.

sets.g: FamilySearch · Transvaal probate index, by collection
sets.n: searching the index instead of guessing the film
rows: The whole indexed surname in one Transvaal collection, read in two pages of a hundred and fifty. Confirms the Stephanus Francois file (1940) and the Jan Gerhardus Lodewikus file, and shows that the 1946–1957 estates this archive is chasing are NOT name-indexed — they will have to be found by browsing film.

TAB MHG 1928/42 in full: Joseph Heinrich Daschner, his parents, his wife “born Booyzen”, and eleven children. Read from the image, not the index — the index gives one child's birth year as 1923 where the document says 1922.

Useless as run: the engine treats Mountjoy as fuzzy and returns every Montgomery, Montjoy and Montmorency in the Transvaal. Recorded because the failure is instructive — an exact-match toggle exists for surnames in this API and not for given names.

Charles Bruce Rennie, miner, of Booysens, Johannesburg, died 1936; his pre-deceased wife was a Minnie Bertha Sophia Daschner. No Booyzen connection. Kept as the archive's cleanest example of the Booysens-suburb trap.

sets.g: FamilySearch · Transvaal probate, reading the whole surname
sets.n: what happens when you stop searching for a person and search for a name
rows: BOOYSEN + PETRUS JACOBUS, exact surname, collection 2520237

Sterfkennis No. 678 of 1876 — Petrus Jacobus Booijsen, b. Graaffreinet, d. 1 Sep 1876 district Rustenburg, aged 88, parents NAMED. The oldest document this archive has read, and it was sitting in a name index the whole time. Found only because the search stopped asking for the nine references NAAIRS had given and started reading the surname.
BOOYZEN, exact surname, same collection, second page of results
Two more notices read in full

Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen (d. 1920, Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg), whose father is entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen; and Anna Johanna Booijzen, born Cradock about 1823, died 1891 on a farm in the district of Rustenburg, with children called Petrus Jacobus, Magdalena Johanna and Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas. Right names, right districts, right decades. NEITHER WAS PROVED TO BE KIN when this was written — and the second of them SINCE HAS BEEN. The farm is BRAKFONTEIN, not Boekfontein, and the maiden name is OLIEFIER, not Alberts: she is Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier, the first wife of Hendrik Stefanus Booijsen, and she died on the family's own farm.
TAB MHG O/2899 — Jan Gerhardus Lodewikus Booyzen, 1885

The persona indexed under that name in the Transvaal probate collection turned out to be a FATHER named on somebody else’s 1920 death notice, not the 1885 estate. The NAAIRS reference stands and is still unread. Recorded because the two were briefly conflated here.

sets.g: FamilySearch · Cape probate, the whole surname at once
sets.n: the same method, turned on the Cape
rows: Everything this archive was still chasing in the Cape, on one screen. Estate 58379 and 58380 read in full; the 1840 James Montjoy notice re-identified in the same list; and Hercules Johannes’s single hit opened and found to be his mother-in-law’s.
One hit, and it is not his
His name is on his mother-in-law’s 1902 notice, in her list of children. The index keys every name on the page. Confirms rather than overturns this archive’s finding that he has no estate file.

Not a name search at all. Once the film and image number were known, the pages either side of a death notice could be read in sequence — which is how the liquidation and distribution accounts were found. This is the route to the six Transvaal estates that are not name-indexed.

sets.g: The register, used as a search tool for the first time
sets.n: one word typed into the filter
rows: A Willem Hermanus Booijzen taking church membership at Indwe in 1907, and two Booyzen children baptised there in 1908 and 1910 — two and five years after the Willem Hermanus this archive had dying at Indwe in 1905. All four read from the register images. The register was built to hold leads; this is the first one it handed over.
FamilySearch, South Africa, Civil Marriage Records — BOOYZEN + ROODT
Indwe, 21 September 1908, certificate 13. The document that carries the word MIJNWERKER.
Booyzen + Roodt, any later marriage or death
No death record and no second marriage found for Willem Hermanus Booyzen of Indwe, and nothing yet for either Roodt woman after 1910. The Indwe registers past 1910 have not been read forward.

sets.g: The Transvaal probate index, read against itself
sets.n: no new document — an index line and two already read
rows: TAB MHG O/2899 — who is actually the deceased?
Jan Gerardus Lodewicus Booijzen, 67, b. district Graaff-Reinet, d. 25 May 1885 Vaalbank

Two index passes over the same estate (arks 1:1:QPTJ-R6KB and 1:1:Q2DG-52P9) agree, and one of them states the relationship: Deceased. Born about 1818, so not the nephew born in 1855 this archive had attached it to for months.

The FamilySearch record page says “Check Image Availability” where every other estate in this archive says “View original document”. The file is at the Transvaal Archives in Pretoria and has not been seen. The correction above rests on the index, checked against the 1876 and 1920 Sterfkennisse, both read from the image.
Any death record for Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booysen, b. 4 Dec 1855
With the estate taken off him there is no date and no place. Recorded as an open name rather than a closed life.

sets.g: FamilySearch · can the last six Transvaal estates be read at all?
sets.n: a negative with its scope written down
rows: Film access across the whole collection, 762 films, 007805260 to 007831001

Twenty-eight films from 007830063 onward were requested and twenty-eight returned HTTP 403. Those are the films whose indexed records reach 1946 and later. Film 007830062, the one immediately before the line, serves its images normally. This is an access boundary, not a gap in the index.
Nothing to be done from here. The originals are at the Transvaal Archives Depot in Pretoria.
TAB MHG 52653 (1923) — in the open half

Not name-indexed under any spelling of Booyzen, Booysen or Booijzen. And the films are NOT ordered by estate number: image 100 of three films in the same numeric neighbourhood produced a 1920 Sterfkennis, a 1938 death notice, and a Chinese clan genealogy. The interpolation trick that found the 1840 Montjoy notice has nothing to interpolate along here.
Works alone; silently ignored with a surname

Recorded because it nearly produced a false negative. q.filmNumber=007830063 alone returns 211 personas. Add q.surname=Booyzen and the result is 150 — which is the count for the surname across the WHOLE collection. The film filter is dropped without a word. Any search combining the two is a search of the whole collection wearing a disguise.

sets.g: FamilySearch · the whole BOOYZEN surname in the CAPE probate collection
sets.n: twenty-nine people, and the z spelling is the Master's own
rows: 29 personas — small enough to read entire

The Transvaal collection holds 150 under this spelling; the Cape holds 29. Two of them are estate 84992 of 1943 — Isabella Fredrika Booyzen born Coetzee, and her husband and son — and the file is spelled with a z by the Master's office throughout.
Corrected a date this archive had taken off the reference number. Also gave her parents, her three children, and the death of a son it had been carrying as living.
The oldest Booyzen in the Cape probate series

Johanna Booyzen, born about 20 March 1754, died 16 June 1843 at Cape Town. Read because her dates match the only two this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer. They match to the year and she is somebody else entirely.

Neither is name-indexed. The Cape films carry readable target boards — DEATH NOTICES, or DECEASED ESTATES with a year and a starting estate number — and every 19th-century board read so far says DEATH NOTICES. The separate wills and liquidation-account volumes are not evidently in this collection at all. The catalogue, which would settle it, is blocked to this archive: every catalog API path returns 403 from FamilySearch's security service.

sets.g: The Marico question, tested on names
sets.n: no new search — the data this archive already holds, put against itself
rows: The seven TAB CJC compensation claims, by initials, against the eight children on the 1876 Sterfkennis

JPJ, PJ, GL, JPJ, L, JC, HE against David Schalk, Magdalena Johanna, Petrus Jacobus, Anna Eliezabet, Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus, Eliezabet Cornelia, Hendrik Stefanus, Anna Maria. PJ, GL and L fit; JPJ, JC and HE do not. With a family this repetitive about forenames that is roughly what chance gives you, and by 1903 the 1876 children were dead or in their eighties — a real claimant would be a grandson, a generation beyond what this archive can name.
Where the Marico JPJ was born

The index gives the man behind two of the seven claims as born at Pietermaritzburg and dead at Rhenosterfontein, district Marico, in November 1900. This family is Graaff-Reinet. It is the one hard fact in the comparison and it points away.

sets.g: NAAIRS · the Cape compensation series, found and then tested
sets.n: the burned-farm question, taken as far as a keyboard can take it
rows: What IS the Cape equivalent of the Transvaal CJC?

Named at last. KAB, source NA, volume 564, reference A1068: “War Losses Compensation Commission, Sub-Commissioners Captain E. J. Whindus and Mr H. H. Bunn”, 1902. This archive has been asking for “Cape Colony compensation claims” for weeks without knowing what they were called.
KAB · BOOYZEN and BOOYSEN against COMPENSATION and LOSSES

BOOYZEN returns 39 documents in the Cape depot and none of them mention compensation or losses. BOOYSEN returns 2,370 and exactly one in combination: a Workmen's Compensation Act 1941 claim at King William's Town, 1947–49, naming D. B. Booysen. Nothing to do with the war.
The control — is the Commission indexed by claimant at all?
NO, AND THE ZERO ABOVE IS THEREFORE WEAK

SMIT, SCHOEMAN and BARRY also return nothing under LOSSES in the Cape depot. The two BOTHA hits are a 1935 locust and arsenical-poisoning stock claim from a magistrate's series. The Commission's records are catalogued by sub-commissioner and volume, not by the people who claimed. A name search cannot reach them, so a name search finding nothing means very little.

Recorded because it silently manufactures false negatives. BOOY* in the Cape depot returns 0 documents. BOOYZEN, spelled out, returns 39. Four searches run here with an asterisk were discarded and re-run. Anyone using NAAIRS should assume the wildcard does not expand.
The bare hostname no longer resolves

national.archsrch.gov.za does not resolve at all. www.national.archsrch.gov.za does, and is the address the National Archives' own help page links to. Noted because the database on which much of this archive rests appears dead if you type it from memory.

sets.g: The Cape Master's Index of Estates, 1834–1912 — read at Barry
sets.n: film 007844477, pages 232 to 234, located by bisection
rows: Three pages, and this family on none of them

The index is alphabetical with the death-notice number beside each name. Barry runs 232–234. Not Richard Peter, not Frederick Fortunatus, not Dorothea Regina, not Hendrik Nicholaas, not Kathleen Mary, not Catherine Maria Sophia — and not John Augustus, who died in 1903, or Margaretha, who died in 1912.
Why the absence is not an absence

This archive has already read them. The index closes in 1912 and they were filed in 1915 — twelve years after John Augustus died. The estate route to identifying the Cape Rebel Richard Peter Barry is therefore closed for this period, not merely empty.

Film 007844477 runs to 612 images and carries no name index of its own. Its length was found by bisection, then page numbers were read off the top of a sample — about 1.9 pages per image — and Barry was reached in four rounds: images 20, 35, 50, 65, then 85, 95, 105, then 112, 117, 122, then 125. Recorded because it is the technique that will be needed again.

sets.g: FamilySearch · the Indwe congregation, and Barkly East by place
sets.n: items 5, 10 and 11 of the standing list
rows: Johanna Catharina Mountjoy, membership Indwe 23 July 1907
Lidmaten register page 336: arrived FROM BARKLY OOST on 23 July 1907, and the remarks column records her dead at Indwe in June 1911.
Willem Hermanus Booyzen of Indwe, after September 1910
No third baptism, no later marriage, no death in the Dutch Reformed index. He is twenty-four at his daughter's baptism and then gone from anything this archive can reach.
BARRY ranked by place — Barkly East

q.anyPlace does not filter but it does rank, and the right Barrys come to the top. Richard Pieter Kolbe Barry (b. 1899), James Henry (c.1847–1939), Harriet Louisa of Manorowen (d. 1912), Cornelia Herculena Petronella of Cherryville (d. 1909), John Gerson Eliazer (1893–1941), Theunis Christoffel (1895–1963). All index entries, none read from an image, and every person page says so.
Where John Barry's 1915 estate was administered
A second and independent reason why no member of this family appears in the Cape Master's Index of Estates 1834–1912.

sets.g: FamilySearch · the Cape civil death registers, Barkly East
sets.n: the Barry thread, opened by the Grahamstown discovery
rows: “Irishman born in Ireland.” Carpenter. Manor Owen Ward IV. 25 August 1903. Eleven children. Signed by Richard Barry, son present at death. Answers open question 5 and corrects two things this archive had published.

Of Manorowen, dead of typhoid at Cherryville aged eighteen, buried at Manorowen, her father H. N. Barry signing. Entered as DUTCH. Confirms Cherryville as a third Barry farm and dates the family's assimilation to one generation.
RICHARD PIETER KOLBE BARRY — whose son?
Richard Pieter Barry and Jeannie Maria Catharina Botha

Baptised at Barkly West, 26 April 1898. It does not prove the father is the Richard Peter Barry on the Cape Rebel roll, but it puts a married Richard Peter Barry with children in that district in 1898.
The children of Hendrik Nicholaas Barry and Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman

Ruben Jacobus Hosea (Dordrecht, 1888), Dorothea Regina (Slang River, 1892), Henriette Louisa (Barkly West, 1894) and Ellen Hendrika (1900). Two are named for their aunt and uncle, which is why this archive now carries two Dorothea Reginas and two Rubens and keeps them apart.

sets.g: An audit of this archive's own negatives
sets.n: checking whether the wildcard fault had contaminated anything already published
rows: Every search recorded on this site, checked for an asterisk

The NAAIRS wildcard returns zero rather than expanding, which would silently turn any wildcard search into a false negative. Every row on this page and every query in the working notes was re-read. The only asterisk in the notes is markdown emphasis. No negative published by this archive was built with one.
Hendrik Stephanus found; the others not yet

David Schalk, Magdalena Johanna, Anna Eliezabet, Eliezabet Cornelia and Anna Maria remain unsearched or unfound. Their brother's estate turned out to carry their mother's name, so the rest are worth the same effort.
Johanna Catharina Mountjoy, died Indwe June 1911
Not in the Cape civil death index
The church register records her death; the civil index does not return her under Mountjoy or Montjoy at Indwe or Wodehouse. Recorded as a scoped negative.
A large family, and the two mothers not separable yet

The Indwe registers carry Roodt baptisms through 1906–1926 under Jan Gabriel, Hermanus Johannes, Andries Johannes Taylor and Pieter Johannes. A Susanna Adrana Elizabeth Roodt was baptised at Indwe on 19 September 1908 and a Cornelis de Klerk Roodt on 31 May 1907. Which household the two mothers of 1908 and 1909 belong to is not yet established.

sets.g: Grahamstown, the depot nobody had searched
sets.n: items 1 to 3 of the standing list
rows: John Barry's 1915 estate, 925 — the whole page

Film 007810152, image 228. Eight children named, against eleven on the 1903 registration. Two of this archive's people withdrawn as children and re-placed as grandchildren. Margaretha Kolbe's death dated to 2 August 1912. The marriage placed at “Burghersdorp (probably)”.
The estates either side of it on the same film
Images 229, 230 and 231 are Louw, van der Vyver and van Zyl — the estate numbers 926, 927 and 928 run consecutively and the Barry file is a single page. There is no liquidation account bound with it.
Her notice is said to have been filed the same day by another son. It is not on the images either side of 925 and has not been found.
